Title: Confirm a response with an undeclared field is caught as a contract break
Preconditions: The service is running and publishes its OpenAPI document.
Steps: 1. Request GET /openapi.json and read the schema for a created change. 2. POST /changes with a complete submission body. 3. Add a field to the returned record that the schema does not declare. 4. Validate the altered record against the schema.
Expected Result: The altered record fails validation with 201 recorded for the original response, proving the schema refuses fields it does not declare.

Title: Confirm a created change matches what the spec promises
Preconditions: The service is running and publishes its OpenAPI document.
Steps: 1. Request GET /openapi.json. 2. POST /changes with a complete submission body. 3. Validate the returned record against the schema the document declares for a 201 response.
Expected Result: The service returns 201 and the record matches the published schema field for field.

Title: Confirm every error the spec lists describes the body it returns
Preconditions: The service is running and publishes its OpenAPI document.
Steps: 1. Request GET /openapi.json. 2. List every response in the 400 and 500 ranges that the document declares. 3. Check each one names a body schema.
Expected Result: The document returns 200 and every declared error response carries a body schema, so a consumer can write error handling against it.

Title: Confirm every operation the spec lists is named
Preconditions: The service is running and publishes its OpenAPI document.
Steps: 1. Request GET /openapi.json. 2. Read every documented operation. 3. Check each one carries a summary.
Expected Result: The document returns 200 and no operation is unnamed.

Title: Confirm the health response matches what the spec promises
Preconditions: The service is running and publishes its OpenAPI document.
Steps: 1. Request GET /openapi.json and read the schema for the health response. 2. Request GET /healthz. 3. Validate the response against that schema.
Expected Result: The health endpoint returns 200 and the body matches the published schema.

Title: Confirm a refused transition matches what the spec promises
Preconditions: The service is running and publishes its OpenAPI document.
Steps: 1. Request GET /openapi.json. 2. POST /changes to create a change in Draft. 3. Request a transition straight to Closed. 4. Validate the refusal body against the schema declared for a 409.
Expected Result: The transition is refused with 409 and the refusal body matches the published schema, including the rule and the states involved.

Title: Confirm a not found response matches what the spec promises
Preconditions: The service is running and publishes its OpenAPI document.
Steps: 1. Request GET /openapi.json. 2. Request GET /changes/does-not-exist. 3. Validate the response against the schema declared for a 404.
Expected Result: The service returns 404 and the body matches the published schema.

Title: Confirm a change read back matches what the spec promises
Preconditions: The service is running and publishes its OpenAPI document.
Steps: 1. Request GET /openapi.json. 2. POST /changes with a complete submission body. 3. Read the change back with GET /changes/{id}. 4. Validate the response against the published schema.
Expected Result: The read returns 200 and the record matches the published schema, which is a different code path from the one that created it.

Title: Confirm a refused submission matches what the spec promises
Preconditions: The service is running and publishes its OpenAPI document.
Steps: 1. Request GET /openapi.json. 2. POST /changes with a submission that has no rollback plan and no Jira ticket. 3. Submit it. 4. Validate the refusal body against the schema declared for a 400.
Expected Result: The submission is refused with 400 and the refusal body matches the published schema, so a consumer can read the violations programmatically.

Title: Confirm a malformed request error matches what the spec promises
Preconditions: The service is running and publishes its OpenAPI document.
Steps: 1. Request GET /openapi.json. 2. POST /changes with a body that is missing most required fields. 3. Validate the error against the schema declared for a 422.
Expected Result: The service returns 422 and the body matches the published schema for a validation error.

Title: Confirm an accepted submission matches what the spec promises
Preconditions: The service is running and publishes its OpenAPI document.
Steps: 1. Request GET /openapi.json. 2. POST /changes with a complete submission body. 3. Submit it. 4. Validate the returned record against the published schema.
Expected Result: The submission is accepted with 200 and the record matches the published schema.

Title: Confirm the spec version matches the version the service is running
Preconditions: The service is running.
Steps: 1. Request GET /openapi.json and read the version in the document. 2. Compare it with the version the service reports.
Expected Result: The document returns 200 and the version in it matches the version the service runs, so the published description cannot drift from the build.

Title: Confirm the service publishes a spec a consumer can code against
Preconditions: The service is running.
Steps: 1. Request GET /openapi.json. 2. Read the OpenAPI version and the service title.
Expected Result: The service returns 200 and publishes an OpenAPI 3.1 document titled Release Gate API.

Title: Cancel a scheduled change before implementation starts
Preconditions: The service is running. A change request has been created and submitted.
Steps: 1. Create a change and submit it. 2. Transition it to Approved. 3. Transition it to Scheduled. 4. Transition it to Cancelled. 5. Read the change back.
Expected Result: Each transition returns 200 and the change reads back as cancelled, because cancellation is allowed at any point before implementation starts.

Title: Read back a change that was just created
Preconditions: The service is running.
Steps: 1. POST /changes with a complete submission body and note the identifier returned. 2. Request GET /changes/{id} with that identifier.
Expected Result: The read returns 200 and the record carries the same submission that was sent, so what was written is what is read.

Title: Cancel a change after implementation has started
Preconditions: The service is running. A change request has reached Implementing.
Steps: 1. Create a change, submit it, and transition it through Approved and Scheduled to Implementing. 2. Request a transition to Cancelled.
Expected Result: The transition is refused with 409 naming REQ-2.1, because a change cannot be cancelled once implementation has started.

Title: Submit the same change twice
Preconditions: The service is running. A change request has been created and submitted once.
Steps: 1. Create a change with a complete submission body. 2. Submit it and confirm it is accepted. 3. Submit the same change a second time.
Expected Result: The second submission is refused with 409, because the change is no longer in Draft.

Title: Submit a change with no BAT test evidence
Preconditions: The service is running. Testing evidence is available for dev and QA but not for BAT.
Steps: 1. POST /changes with evidence for dev and QA only. 2. Submit the change.
Expected Result: The submission is refused with 400 and the violation names REQ-1.2, because evidence in all three environments is required.

Title: Submit a change with a timestamp that has no timezone
Preconditions: The service is running.
Steps: 1. POST /changes with a complete submission body, but give implementation_start a timestamp with no timezone.
Expected Result: The service returns 422 rather than 400, because the request could not be read at all rather than being read and refused by a rule.

Title: Create a change request with a complete submission
Preconditions: The service is running.
Steps: 1. POST /changes with a complete submission body.
Expected Result: The service returns 201 with the change record, an identifier, and a state of draft.

Title: Submit a change that breaks three gate rules at once
Preconditions: The service is running. A submission is missing its rollback plan, its Jira ticket and all testing evidence.
Steps: 1. POST /changes with those three things missing. 2. Submit the change. 3. Read the change back.
Expected Result: The submission is refused with 400 listing all three violations at once, and the change reads back still in draft rather than advanced.

Title: Submit a single page app release with no Prod Support on call
Preconditions: The service is running. The release type is a single page app with DevOps and Tech Lead on call and no Prod Support.
Steps: 1. POST /changes declaring release type spa with only those two roles on call. 2. Submit the change.
Expected Result: The submission is accepted with 200, because the on call matrix does not require Prod Support for a single page app release.

Title: Submit a change that meets every gate rule
Preconditions: The service is running. A submission meets every gate rule.
Steps: 1. POST /changes with a complete submission body. 2. Submit the change. 3. Read the change back.
Expected Result: The submission is accepted with 200 and the change reads back as submitted.

Title: Move a change backwards from Implementing to Approved
Preconditions: The service is running. A change request has reached Implementing.
Steps: 1. Create a change, submit it, and transition it through Approved and Scheduled to Implementing. 2. Request a transition back to Approved.
Expected Result: The transition is refused with 409 naming REQ-2.2, because there is no route back once implementation has started.

Title: Read a change that does not exist
Preconditions: The service is running. No change exists with the identifier used below.
Steps: 1. Request GET /changes/ with an identifier that was never created.
Expected Result: The service returns 404 with a machine readable code of not_found.

Title: Submit a change with a field the API does not define
Preconditions: The service is running.
Steps: 1. POST /changes with a complete submission body and one extra field the API does not define, such as approved_by.
Expected Result: The service returns 422 and refuses the request, rather than accepting it and silently dropping the field.

Title: Request a transition to a state the API does not define
Preconditions: The service is running. A change request exists in Draft.
Steps: 1. Create a change. 2. Request a transition to a state the API does not define, such as shipped.
Expected Result: The service returns 422 from the schema rather than 409 from the lifecycle, because the value is not a state at all.

Title: Close a change straight from Implementing without rolling back
Preconditions: The service is running. A change request has reached Implementing.
Steps: 1. Create a change, submit it, and transition it through Approved and Scheduled to Implementing. 2. Request a transition straight to Closed. 3. Request a transition to Rolled Back.
Expected Result: The move to Closed is refused with 409 naming REQ-2.3, and the move to Rolled Back is accepted with 200, because failed verification rolls back rather than closing.

Title: Health check on a running service
Preconditions: The service is running.
Steps: 1. Request GET /healthz.
Expected Result: The service returns 200 with a status of ok and the version it is running.

Title: Submit a change that does not exist
Preconditions: The service is running. No change exists with the identifier used below.
Steps: 1. POST /changes/{id}/submit using an identifier that was never created.
Expected Result: The service returns 404 rather than attempting to validate a change that does not exist.

Title: Walk a change through every state from Draft to Closed
Preconditions: The service is running. A submission meets every gate rule.
Steps: 1. Create a change and submit it. 2. Transition it in turn to Approved, Scheduled, Implementing, Verified and Closed.
Expected Result: Every transition returns 200 and the change ends in closed, with each state persisted so the next request sees what the previous one wrote.

Title: Request a transition on a change that does not exist
Preconditions: The service is running. No change exists with the identifier used below.
Steps: 1. POST /changes/{id}/transition using an identifier that was never created.
Expected Result: The service returns 404.

Title: Advance one change and confirm a second is unaffected
Preconditions: The service is running.
Steps: 1. Create two separate change requests. 2. Submit the first one only. 3. Read both back.
Expected Result: The first reads back as submitted and the second as draft, so the two records do not share state.

Title: Move a draft straight to Submitted, bypassing the gate rules
Preconditions: The service is running. A change request exists in Draft with no rollback plan.
Steps: 1. Create a change with no rollback plan. 2. Request a transition straight to Submitted, bypassing the submit endpoint. 3. Read the change back.
Expected Result: The transition is refused with 409 and a code of validation_required, and the change reads back still in draft, so the gate rules cannot be stepped around.

Title: Create a change while the database is unavailable
Preconditions: The service is running. The database it writes to is unavailable.
Steps: 1. Make the database unavailable to the running service. 2. POST /changes with a complete submission body.
Expected Result: The service returns 500 rather than reporting success, so a caller is never told a change was recorded when it was not.

Title: Submit a change whose implementation window ends before it starts
Preconditions: The service is running. A submission carries an implementation window that ends before it starts.
Steps: 1. POST /changes with implementation_start set four hours after implementation_end. 2. Submit the change.
Expected Result: The submission is refused with 400 naming the reversed window. This case currently fails: the gate accepts it and returns 200. Tracked as DEF-002 and deferred to 0.2.0.
